title: Horizontal Pod Autoscaler
description: Automatically scale application Pods up or down based on CPU, memory, or custom metrics using Kubernetes Horizontal Pod Autoscaler.

data.text: What Is the Horizontal Pod Autoscaler?

The **Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA)** automatically adjusts the number of Pod replicas in a Deployment, StatefulSet, or ReplicaSet based on observed CPU utilization, memory usage, or custom metrics. Instead of manually scaling your application during peak traffic or quiet periods, the HPA monitors metrics and scales your workload up or down to match demand — saving resources and maintaining performance.

HPA is a Kubernetes resource in the `autoscaling/v2` API group. It polls the Metrics Server (or a custom metrics adapter) every 15 seconds by default, compares the current metric value to the target you set, and calculates the desired replica count. If the desired count differs from the current count, the HPA updates the underlying ReplicaSet.

terms.definition: Automatically scales the number of Pod replicas based on observed metrics.
A cluster-wide aggregator of resource usage data; provides CPU and memory metrics to the HPA.
Application-specific metrics (e.g., requests per second) from Prometheus or other adapters.
Metrics from outside the cluster, such as SQS queue depth or CloudWatch alarms.
The HPA reducing the number of Pod replicas when demand decreases.

data.text: CPU-based autoscaling is the simplest form. You tell the HPA to maintain a target CPU utilization percentage across all Pods. For example, if you set the target to 70% and your Pods are averaging 90% CPU, the HPA adds more replicas to bring the average down. If utilization drops to 30%, the HPA removes excess replicas.

data.title: HPA targeting 70% CPU utilization
data.content: Scale a Deployment between 2 and 10 replicas based on CPU usage.
data.code:
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: api-hpa
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: api-deployment
  minReplicas: 2
  maxReplicas: 10
  metrics:
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: cpu
      target:
        type: Utilization
        averageUtilization: 70

data.text: CPU and memory are useful, but real-world scaling often depends on business metrics. An API might need to scale based on requests per second, a message consumer based on queue depth, or a video encoder based on job backlog. Kubernetes supports **custom metrics** (from Prometheus, Datadog, etc.) and **external metrics** (from cloud services or databases) through metric adapters.

data.title: HPA using custom Prometheus metrics
data.content: Scale based on HTTP requests per second from Prometheus.
data.code:
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: api-hpa
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: api-deployment
  minReplicas: 2
  maxReplicas: 20
  metrics:
  - type: Pods
    pods:
      metric:
        name: http_requests_per_second
      target:
        type: AverageValue
        averageValue: 1000m

data.title: Always set minReplicas and maxReplicas
data.text: Without maxReplicas, the HPA can scale indefinitely during a traffic spike, exhausting cluster capacity. Without minReplicas, your application might scale to zero and become unavailable.

HPAs do not react instantly. The default polling interval is 15 seconds, and there is a cool-down period before scaling down to prevent flapping. You can tune these with `--horizontal-pod-autoscaler-sync-period` on the controller manager and the `behavior` section in the HPA spec.

rows: Prevents flapping by using the highest desired scale from a recent window

data.title: Configure HPA for an API Deployment
data.description: Set up CPU-based and custom metric autoscaling.
steps: Ensure Metrics Server is installed in your cluster.
Deploy an API Deployment with CPU requests set to 200m.
Create an HPA targeting 60% CPU utilization with minReplicas=2 and maxReplicas=10.
Generate load with a stress test tool or kubectl run.
Watch the HPA scale up: kubectl get hpa -w.
Stop the load and observe the HPA scale down after the stabilization window.
data.expectedOutcome: The HPA automatically adds replicas under load and removes them when traffic drops, keeping CPU utilization near target.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: HPA automatically scales Pod replicas based on CPU, memory, or custom metrics.
Metrics Server is required for CPU and memory autoscaling; custom metrics need an adapter.
Always set minReplicas and maxReplicas to bound scaling behavior.
HPAs poll metrics on a schedule and have built-in stabilization to prevent flapping.
Use custom metrics (e.g., requests per second) for business-aware autoscaling.
data.takeaway: HPA lets your cluster automatically match supply to demand, keeping performance high and costs low.
